thread:
incident-bot: Paging oncall -> maria: P1 streaming errors for customer halcyon (dedicated pool cp-hal-02). Symptoms: websocket disconnects, SSE reconnect storms, high 5xx from app gateway. Alert: sustained 4xx/5xx + slow tail latencies. Runbook: https://go/runbooks/streaming.

maria: I'm oncall, looking. halcyon-ops, do you see anything on your side?

halcyon-ops: We started seeing clients reauth + reconnects around 11:07 UTC. App GW logs show repeated 502/504s and KEEPALIVE timeouts in the 20-35s range. No config changes on our side.

ashley: I can see a spike in websocket disconnects in cp-hal-02 at 11:06. P50 OK but p99 token handshake latency jumps to 2.1s and streams drop after ~30s.

raj: Reading infra metrics: our edge LB is showing connection churn and upstream keepalives to the customer's appgw are failing. CPU on the gateway nodes hasn't spiked, but we have a backlog on the streaming ingress queue. Possibly backpressure/slow consumer.

maria: Key question: is this client-side idle timeout or server-side inability to drain? Can we correlate client IPs to specific halcyon shards?

ashley: Running quick grep on appgw logs:
```
11:06:12 halcyon-appgw-03 stream_conn_id=abc123 status=502 upstream=timeout idle_timeout=30s
11:06:14 halcyon-appgw-04 stream_conn_id=def456 status=504 upstream=reset read_timeout=32s
```
Looks like upstream read/idle timeouts hitting.

maria: Mitigation idea 1: increase appgw idle timeout temporarily to 90s and enable websocket ping/pong at the proxy layer so slow clients don't drop. Need halcyon-ops consent. Mitigation idea 2: route halcyon traffic to dedicated-fallback pool cp-hal-fallback while we investigate — will preserve connection state? fallback is stateless, you'll lose in-flight contexts.

halcyon-ops: We can increase idle timeout. We need confirmation on client reconnect behavior if we route to fallback. Also concerned about tenant isolation — don't want other customers affected.

raj: We can apply strict routing rule for prefix "customer=halcyon" to only move their traffic. That keeps tenant isolation. Doing a gradual 5% shift to fallback will limit blast radius.

ashley: I'll push a canary route:
```
route add --pool cp-hal-fallback --match "customer=halcyon" --weight 5%
```
Monitoring will be on for 2m before stepping to 20%.

maria: Also enabling prefix/KV cache bypass for halcyon requests to avoid stale prefixes causing long compute times:
```
service-config: halcyon.cache_mode: bypass
```
This should reduce initial model warmups causing long tail latencies.

incident-bot: Action created -> INC-2026-987: Route canary + appgw timeout increase. Assigned to ashley, raj.

ashley: Canary 5% routing applied at 11:18. Initial metrics: dropped 5xx by ~18% on cp-hal-02, but overall connection churn persists. Stepping to 20%.

halcyon-ops: We've increased appgw keepalive to 90s and enabled ping/pong on proxy. Noticed fewer idle timeouts immediately.

maria: Good. Next step: add transient backpressure response to clients (HTTP 429 with Retry-After) for new connections to avoid retry storms. Can halcyon push that change?

halcyon-ops: Yes we can return 429 on overload. We'll deploy a lightweight rate limiter at the gateway in ~10m.

raj: While that deploys, I'll adjust server-side streaming queue thresholds to drop oldest idle streams (LRU) to free slots for new ones. This is a controlled graceful drop.

ashley: 20% routing live at 11:28. Observed p99 latency down 12%, 5xx down 40% in the canary subset. Overall customer impact reduced but still present.

maria: On-call handoff to L2 (ashley) in 15m for deeper root cause. I'll draft a customer status message for halcyon: short note about temporary mitigations and ETA for further update in 1h.

maria: Message to halcyon-ops sent: "We've applied temporary routing and increased keepalive — you should see fewer disconnects. We're continuing work to stabilize and will follow up in 1h. If you need rollback, tell us now." :thumbsup:

halcyon-ops: Received. Thanks — we'll watch client behavior and the rate limiter rollout.

incident-bot: Update recorded INC-2026-987 -> mitigation applied: canary routing, appgw timeout increase, cache bypass, queue LRU eviction.

ashley: L2 takeover now. I'll keep the incident open and collect traces for postmortem. Items for follow-up: confirm root cause (slow upstream auth validation vs model warmup), validate fallback semantics for in-flight streams, add automated detection for streaming idle storms.

maria: Thanks team. I'll mark as mitigated for customer impact but not resolved. Handoff complete to ashley (L2). Please leave notes in the runbook and tag postmortem owners.

ashley: Acknowledged. Tagging @raj for infra changes and @maria for incident comms.

maria: Closing paging for oncall. Last update 11:40 UTC.
